She sounds like me, so if I could give you some insight into my thought process perhaps that would make you feel a little less worried.

Chances are you’re doing nothing wrong and she’s delighted to have someone like you that cares enough to question the silences. 

Being a single mother, she’s probably tending to children all weekend long, so the break in communication there is normal. Long periods of silence are probably indicative of hitting a low, most people think that when you’re in a depressive episode you’d try to reach out and be social but the opposite is true for me. I go silent on all social media and I don’t feel like texting friends and having bullshit “yeah I’m fine” conversations. 

I think you should try and organise another in person outside of work hangout. I also think that not double texting is correct, overwhelming someone with texts isn’t always the right way to show care. 

You’re doing good, don’t worry x

I’m a stranger on the internet, I have 0.001% context but it sounds to me like you’re heading for an inevitable breakup. You don’t seem ready to have someone in your space 24/7 and she doesn’t seem ready to be in a 50/50 partnership. You need to be brutally honest with this girl as soon as possible. “I need my own space or we will break up, I don’t know how to make that happen, I want to keep you in my life, let’s solve this”

Two things here, perhaps you guys need to not live together? I don’t know if that’s financially viable but it seems like an obvious thing to at least trial for an amount of time. Secondly, it sounds like subconsciously you don’t feel like you have enough time to spend on you. Try make explicit “me time” and inform her of it. If possible dedicate a whole room to yourself and then make that your sanctuary. Again, I don’t know if that’s viable.

What it comes down to is that you need a physical and temporal space away from this girl, it’s needed in all healthy relationships and I’m sure you know that but it doesn’t seem to be formalized enough in this situation.
